episode_title: 72. All about Solar Energy with Pascal Rochat

insights.quote: The main difference between fossil fuels and renewables, is that for renewables? Well, the fuel is free. The fuel is free. Nobody can make you pay for the sun or for the wind. And that is changing the full dynamics of the energy market. Because up to now, we're only talking the price of oil, gas and coal, right? So in the future, not only is energy going to be abundant, with most countries becoming independent, but energy will be very cheap and without volatility. Because volatility is not going to be brought in by the machines, by the solar panels or the wind turbines.
insights.summary: Renewable energy's free fuel source creates a fundamentally different market dynamic - abundant, cheap energy without the volatility of fossil fuels
insights.speaker: Pascal Rochat

insights.quote: In my opinion, it's really not a good idea to pick a stock. But of course, some of the good names and the one some of our listeners might know, there is, for example, Solar Edge... Canadian Solar... I would like the listeners to focus on the big story, obviously.
insights.summary: Individual stock picking in rapidly growing but volatile sectors like solar carries significant risk; better to focus on the overall industry theme
insights.speaker: Pascal Rochat

insights.quote: The cost of generating electricity with solar photovoltaics was divided by 10 in 10 years only, roughly between 2009 and 2019 divided by 10. So it means today, on average, in most countries, solar has become the cheapest source of electricity, generating electricity in the range of 4 cents per kilowatt-hours.
insights.summary: Solar costs have declined 90% in a decade, making it the cheapest electricity source globally at about 4 cents per kWh
insights.speaker: Pascal Rochat

summary: Interview with Pascal Rochat about solar energy market dynamics and investment opportunities. Solar costs have declined 90% in a decade, making it the cheapest electricity source globally at 4 cents per kWh. The market is expected to grow from 240 GW installed in 2022 to over 500 GW by 2025 and 1 TW by 2030. Solar could reach 23-25% of world electricity by 2030, making it the largest electricity source. The Active Solar Fund invests across the entire solar value chain with 27 holdings, emphasizing risk-return analysis rather than individual stock picking.
key_takeaways: Solar costs fell 90% from 2009-2019, now cheapest at ~4 cents/kWh
Market expected to grow from 240 GW in 2022 to 1 TW by 2030
Solar could become largest electricity source by 2030 at 23-25% of global generation
Renewables have free fuel, creating non-volatile energy costs
Individual stock picking in solar carries significant risk despite strong sector growth
